The preferredOrder entry follows the sense-inversion-provision ruling:
James 2:10 — 'he has become GUILTY of all' — is an honest lexical match
for the query 'guilty' in its opposite frame: a guilt-burdened searcher
served a verdict with no gospel. Demoted, never forbidden; it may rank,
just never above the no-condemnation answer. Both refs are in the fixture
corpus. (For the query 'guilt' the pair passes vacuously — James 2:10
carries no 'guilt' token — the assertion is live for 'guilty'.)
'shame' is deliberately NOT an alias here — see manifest.md: shame is a
distinct sense (often the abuse survivor's, where 'confess your sins'
would be a sense-inverted answer), and routing it to confession texts is
exactly the wrong-pairing class the audit flagged.
